lesson_title: Interpreting Global Graphs: Linear, Non-Linear, Increasing, Decreasing
hook_text: Your school day, drawn as one line. Up, flat, steeper, flat, down.
clip_script: Draw your own school day as a graph of distance from home against time, without any numbers. You wake up at home: distance zero, a point on the horizontal axis. You walk to the taxi rank at a steady pace: the line rises, straight, because every minute you are the same bit further away. You wait at the rank: the line is horizontal — time passes, you are not moving. The taxi takes you to school, fast: the line rises again, steeper than the walking part, because a taxi covers more ground per minute than your legs. At school all day: a long horizontal line, far from home. After school you walk to a friend's house in the direction of home but not all the way: the line falls, because you are getting closer to home, and stops at a level above zero. You stay there: horizontal. Then your parent fetches you by car: the line falls steeply to zero. Home.
visual_style: A distance-from-home axis against a time axis; a single line drawing itself through a school day, each segment appearing as the matching scene plays in a corner
call_to_action: Open the full session to read and sketch global graphs of any situation.
